question: Can a colour-blind semantic nearest-case rule recover enough of BL8's evaluator Oracle to select BL5 only for similar photographs while otherwise hard-falling back to AO6?

cases.population: the 17 BL8 sources after their promotion test is closed
cases.label: candidate-majority if BL5 received at least two of three mapping-sealed autonomous choices; otherwise AO6
cases.evaluation_utility: sum of the three already-frozen per-source choices won by the selected arm

feature_model.input: decoded source luma replicated to RGB before fixed DINO normalization
feature_model.feature: L2-normalized mean of the 16x16 patch tokens; no colour, target, arm output or label enters the feature

selector.distance: cosine distance between fixed normalized semantic features
selector.rule: select the held source's single nearest development case label; ties break by source_id; AO6 is the explicit negative label and fallback

controls.evaluator_oracle: post-hoc better arm per source using the same three frozen choices
controls.negative_control: same features and leave-one-out rule under 256 deterministic label permutations preserving five positive cases

branches.pass: retain a development-only semantic hard-case selector and acquire a genuinely new confirmation population before any promotion
branches.fail: close this top-1 retrieval rule and retain AO6; do not tune k, embedding, labels, thresholds or candidate strength on BL8
branches.oracle_only: record product-value heterogeneity but close retrieval when the source-only rule misses the gate

forbidden_actions: read target/reference pixels or hidden grade truth as a feature
use BL8 output colour or candidate diagnostics as selector inputs
change k, model, pooling, distance, labels, thresholds or seed after the report
call source similarity a film mode, stock identity or physical-condition inference
train a neural renderer or directly generate final RGB
promote without a disjoint fresh-population confirmation
claim_ceiling: development-only autonomous preference-routing evidence for two fixed film-inspired explicit looks using colour-blind source semantics; not population preference, film mode, stock response, calibrated operator, authenticity or product promotion
